final_writeup:
I prove a strict, explicit pointwise improvement over the classical √p bound for every admissible prime. Put d=(p−1)/2, q=(√p+1)/2, R=(p+3)/4, and η₀=2p^(−R)R^(−R(p−2)). Then

SOS_4(G_p) ≤ 1 + d/(q+η₀) = √p − dη₀/[q(q+η₀)] < √p.

The argument combines affine symmetrization of the moment matrix, rigidity of the negative Paley eigenspace, and quantitative nonvanishing of prime Fourier minors. I also prove the general localization bound SOS_4(G) ≤ 1+max_v SOS_2(G[N(v)]) and the exact special case SOS_4(G_5)=2.

This is not a full resolution: η₀ is approximately exp(−O(p² log p)), so the displayed estimate remains asymptotic to √p and supplies no fixed ε>0. It therefore neither proves nor refutes the requested polynomial improvement.

results.claim: The Paley graph G_p is d-regular with d=(p−1)/2; adjacent vertices have (p−5)/4 common neighbors and nonadjacent vertices have (p−1)/4. Its adjacency spectrum is {d, ((−1+√p)/2)^((p−1)/2), ((−1−√p)/2)^((p−1)/2)}.
results.proof_sketch: Let χ be the quadratic character, extended by χ(0)=0. Expanding the indicators of nonzero squares and using Σ_x χ((x−u)(x−v))=−1 for u≠v gives the two common-neighbor counts. Consequently A²=dI+((p−5)/4)A+((p−1)/4)(J−I−A). On the orthogonal complement of the all-ones vector, every eigenvalue satisfies z²+z−(p−1)/4=0. Trace(A)=0 determines the two equal multiplicities.

results.claim: Every feasible degree-four moment matrix may be averaged so that its singleton principal block is N=[[1,a1ᵀ],[a1,aI+bA]], where pa is the objective and b is both the moment and diagonal pair-entry of every edge.
results.proof_sketch: The maps x↦sx+t with s a nonzero square are Paley automorphisms and act transitively on vertices and edges. Averaging the corresponding simultaneous row-column permutations preserves feasibility, PSD, and the objective. Moment consistency gives singleton diagonal a, edge entry b, and zero on nonedges. For an edge e, the singleton-to-e column has value b at both endpoints and vanishes outside the endpoints and their common neighborhood.

results.claim: SOS_2(G_p)=√p, and hence the elementary hierarchy bound gives SOS_4(G_p)≤√p.
results.proof_sketch: Let s=−(√p+1)/2 be the least adjacency eigenvalue. PSD of N gives a+bs≥0 and, on the span of the empty index and 1, a+bd−pa²≥0. Thus b≤a/(−s), whence pa≤1+d/(−s)=√p. Equality is feasible with a=1/√p and b=2/(p+√p): the all-ones Schur complement and the s-eigenspace eigenvalue are zero, while the remaining eigenvalues are nonnegative. Any degree-four matrix has this degree-two principal submatrix.

results.claim: For every finite graph G, SOS_4(G)≤1+max_v SOS_2(G[N(v)]).
results.proof_sketch: Write y_v=Ẽ[x_v] and R_v=Σ_i Ẽ[x_vx_i]. If y_v>0, conditioning by x_v defines a degree-two pseudoexpectation L_v[f]=Ẽ[x_vf]/y_v: positivity follows because Ẽ[x_vq²]=Ẽ[(x_vq)²]≥0 for linear q, using x_v²=x_v. It fixes x_v=1 and is supported on its closed neighborhood, so R_v≤y_v(1+SOS_2(G[N(v)])). If y_v=0, PSD forces R_v=0. Finally, PSD gives (Σ_v y_v)²≤Σ_v R_v. Summing and cancelling the nonnegative objective proves the claim.

results.claim: For nonzero f:F_p→C, |supp(f)|+|supp(f̂)|≥p+1; equivalently, every square minor of the p×p Fourier matrix is nonzero.
results.proof_sketch: Let ζ be a primitive pth root. For distinct row exponents x_i and ordered column exponents y_j, the determinant det(ζ^(x_i y_j)) is a generalized Vandermonde determinant. Divide it by the ordinary Vandermonde in ζ^(x_i). Modulo π=1−ζ, the quotient specializes to ∏_{i<j}(y_j−y_i)/(j−i), which is nonzero in F_p. Hence the determinant is nonzero. If |supp(f)|+|supp(f̂)|≤p, choose |supp(f̂)| zeros of f. The corresponding invertible Fourier minor forces every nonzero Fourier coefficient to vanish, a contradiction.

results.claim: Let P_- project onto the least-eigenvalue Paley eigenspace and let S_e consist of an edge e and all its common neighbors. With R=|S_e|=(p+3)/4, every real f supported on S_e and equal to 1 at both endpoints satisfies ||P_-f||²≥η₀:=2p^(−R)R^(−R(p−2)).
results.proof_sketch: The negative eigenspace consists of one quadratic class of nonzero Fourier frequencies. If P_-f=0, then f̂ has support at most (p+1)/2. Since R+(p+1)/2=(3p+5)/4<p+1, the uncertainty result forces f=0, impossible at the endpoints. Quantitatively, K=P_-[S_e,S_e] is positive definite. Cauchy–Binet expresses det K as p^(−R) times a sum of squared R×R Fourier minors. Choose one minor D. Its cyclotomic field norm is a nonzero integer, while Hadamard bounds every conjugate by R^(R/2); hence |D|≥R^(−R(p−2)/2). Thus det K≥p^(−R)R^(−R(p−2)). All eigenvalues of K are at most 1, so λ_min(K)≥det K. Finally ||f||²≥2.

results.claim: For every prime p≡1 (mod 4), SOS_4(G_p)≤1+d/(q+η₀)<√p, with d=(p−1)/2 and q=(√p+1)/2.
results.proof_sketch: Use the averaged matrix and fix an edge e. Let c be its singleton-to-pair column and δ=a−qb, the singleton-block eigenvalue on the negative Paley eigenspace. The principal PSD block on that eigenspace and pair e gives ||P_-c||²≤bδ. If b>0, c/b is supported on S_e and equals 1 at the endpoints, so the preceding claim gives δ≥bη₀. Hence b≤a/(q+η₀). The empty/all-ones PSD condition gives pa²≤a+db, and therefore pa≤1+d/(q+η₀). If b=0 the stronger pa≤1 holds. Since d/q=√p−1, the bound equals √p−dη₀/[q(q+η₀)], which is strictly smaller than √p.

results.claim: If G is triangle-free and has an edge, then SOS_4(G)=2; in particular SOS_4(G_5)=2.
results.proof_sketch: For distinct edges e,f, their union is not a clique, so the edge-edge principal block is diagonal with entries z_e=M_{∅,e}=M_{e,e}≥0. PSD of the block indexed by the empty set and all edges gives S:=Σ_e z_e≤1. If t is the objective, PSD on the empty and summed-singleton directions gives t²≤Σ_{i,j}M_{i,j}=t+2S≤t+2, hence t≤2. An actual edge supplies a feasible moment matrix of value 2. For p=5 the common-neighbor parameter is zero, so G_5 is triangle-free and nonempty.
